title: Model onboarding CI quicknotes
content:
Purpose:
A compact, practical reference for engineers adding new models to the evals harness. Focus: the small set of scripts, dataset loader shape, scoring functions, and CI checks we iterate on most. This file is intentionally light-weight and action-oriented (notes to self + commands).

Context & goals:
- Goal: make it easy to land a model with minimal friction and high confidence that regressions will be detected by CI.
- Audience: applied-ml engs, onboarding SREs, model owners.
- Scope: baseline evals (lm/text-gen + instruction-following), embedding smoke checks, and regression reports. Not covering massive multi-turn RLHF evals or full A/B experiment infra.

High-level flow (recommended):
1) Add model config (models/<model_name>.yml) with basic metadata + tokenizer hints.
2) Implement loader (evaluations/loaders/<model_name>_loader.py) following Loader API below.
3) Add prompt set under prompts/<model_name>/ (a few small canonical prompts, 50-200 examples for regression).
4) Add scoring hooks in evaluations/scorers/<model_family>_scorers.py if needed (reuse generic scorers first).
5) Create smoke CI job via .github/workflows/evals-<model_name>.yml that runs quick checks on PRs.
6) Full nightly/regression job points to the canonical prompt-set and writes a regression report CSV.

Loader interface (shape we expect) - keep minimal and fast:
- class Loader: 
  - def __init__(self, source: str, split: str = "dev", limit: int | None = None):
      - source: path/url/id for dataset, split: train/dev/test, limit: quick-sampling param.
  - def __iter__(self): yields dict of {"id": str, "input": str, "expected": str | None, "meta": dict}
  - def validate_schema(self) -> list[str]: returns list of problems or empty list.
Notes: Favor deterministic sampling for repeatable CI (seeded). Keep loader fast: avoid heavy preprocessing inside loader; return raw text and put heavy ops in optional transform steps.

Prompt set conventions:
- Directory: prompts/<model_name>/
- Files: 01-instructional.txt, 02-completion-style.txt, 03-embeddings-list.txt (if embeddings), 99-regression-cases.csv
- 99-regression-cases.csv: columns -> id,input,expected,notes. Keep <= 200 rows for onboarding.
- Use short human-readable ids (e.g., conv-001). Include a header comment in txt files describing intent and quality threshold.

Scoring functions: reuse simple, explainable metrics first
- token_overlap (bleu-lite): fraction of overlapping tokens after stopword-strip (good for canonical phrase match).
- answer_match (exact/ci-normalized): lowercased, stripped punctuation, whitespace normalized.
- semantic_sim (embedding-based): cosine similarity using canonical embedder; threshold configurable per task.
- safety_flag_count: heuristic regex-based checks for disallowed content.
Implementation conventions:
- scorer functions are pure and idempotent, return dict: {"score": float, "pass": bool, "reason": str} but for CI we only persist numeric score and pass boolean.
- scoring functions live in evaluations/scorers/*.py and are referenced by name in model config.

CI wiring (PR quickchecks):
- Quickcheck target: run ~20 example prompt-set items through the new model using a fast cached runtime (local container or small hosted token budget).
- GH Action template: .github/workflows/evals-smoke-template.yml
- steps: checkout, setup-python, install evals package, run `python -m evals.cli.run_smoke --model configs/<model>.yml --prompts prompts/<model>/01-instructional.txt --limit 20 --out results/<model>_smoke.json`
- step: `python -m evals.cli.check_regressions --results results/<model>_smoke.json --thresholds configs/<model>_thresholds.yml`
- Exit non-zero on any failing check.
Notes on secrets: tests should use a lightweight test API key for hosted models or a docker-backed local runtime for private models. Avoid using long-lived prod keys in PRs.

Nightly regression job:
- Full prompt set (99-regression-cases.csv) run nightly.
- Output: CSV report with columns -> run_id, model_name, timestamp, prompt_id, score_name, score_value, pass, notes, commit_sha
- Store reports in GCS bucket: gs://redwood-evals/regression-reports/<model_name>/YYYY-MM-DD.csv for historical charts.
- Alerting: create metric (fraction_passed) and attach to Slack channel #ml-evals when pass rate drops > 5% vs baseline for 3 consecutive runs.

Regression report template (CSV header example):
run_id,model_name,timestamp,prompt_id,score_name,score_value,pass,notes,commit_sha
example-run-20240901,redwood-gpt-small,2024-09-01T03:12:22Z,conv-001,semantic_sim,0.82,True,"ok",a1b2c3d

Common gotchas and recommended defaults:
- Tokenizers: always record tokenizer name + version in model config. Small tokenizer differences can flip metrics.
- Determinism: use seeded RNG for any sampling to avoid flakiness in CI.
- Timeout behavior: CI runner should treat timeouts as failures and report latency metric.
- Fuzzy thresholds: store thresholds per-score in configs and allow auto-update requests from owners when evaluating drift.

Quick checklist before PR merge:
- [ ] Loader.validate_schema() returns []
- [ ] Prompt set has at least 10 smoke examples and 50 regression rows (or owner-approved smaller set)
- [ ] Scorers referenced by config exist and are unit-tested
- [ ] CI smoke job passes locally and on PR (use `act` for local GH Action run if needed)
- [ ] Linked PRs/Jira: model onboarding doc + infra ticket

Example minimal model config (YAML, shown inline as text):
---
model_name: redwood-mini
api_type: hosted
tokenizer: sentencepiece-0.1.0
prompts_dir: prompts/redwood-mini
scorers:
  - name: semantic_sim
    threshold: 0.75
  - name: safety_flag_count
    threshold: 0
ci_smoke_limit: 20
---

Local debug commands (useful snippets):
- run single prompt: `python -m evals.cli.run_one --model configs/redwood-mini.yml --prompt prompts/redwood-mini/01-instructional.txt --out /tmp/out.json`
- run smoke: `python -m evals.cli.run_smoke --model configs/redwood-mini.yml --limit 20 --out /tmp/smoke.json`
- check regressions: `python -m evals.cli.check_regressions --results /tmp/smoke.json --thresholds configs/redwood-mini-thresholds.yml`
- generate report CSV from results: `python -m evals.cli.results_to_csv --results /tmp/smoke.json --out /tmp/report.csv`

TODOs (sequenced):
- [ ] Add a small reference implementation for embedding-based semantic_sim in evaluations/scorers/embedding_sim.py (Priya)
- [ ] Add a GH Action template that can run via `workflow_dispatch` for ad-hoc owner-triggered runs (Diego)
- [ ] Document how to plug in Dedicated/private runtime with KMS-backed keys in CI docs page (Riley)

Open questions / discussion points:
- For instruction-following tasks, should we standardize on a single normalization pipeline used by all scorers? (tradeoff: coupling vs consistent metrics)
- Where to store large canonical prompt-sets (git-lfs vs GCS)? Current leaning: small prompt sets in git, larger corpora in gcs + pointer in repo.

References and links:
- evals harness repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals-harness/pull/412
- onboarding Jira epic: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ML-2389
- Confluence page (detailed spec): confluence:applied-ml/onboarding-evals

Notes-to-self:
- When things go flaky, first check tokenizer mismatch + deterministic seed. Second, prioritize reducing test size rather than expanding timeouts.
- Keep smoke job cheap; CI budget is finite.
